McLaren.summary: McLaren has rolled out a fresh front wing and new bodywork over the engine cover to smooth the airflow, plus a tiny winglet on the halo that helps the car stay glued to the track. They’ve also tweaked the rear‑wing endplates, rear‑suspension fairings and floor‑edge devices, and added circuit‑specific cooling louvres to keep the power unit at optimal temperature. All of these changes tighten down‑force and cooling where it counts, giving the team a better grip‑to‑power balance for this weekend’s layout.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has trimmed the height of the outer pieces on the front wing and its end‑plates, giving the car a smoother airflow into the nose and a tighter front‑end feel. They’ve also opened up the side‑cooling ducts and added extra slots on the floor, which helps keep the power unit at its optimum temperature while giving a bit more grip on the low‑speed corners of this circuit. Finally, the rear winglet has been reshaped and repositioned, and the diffuser roof reprofiled, to boost rear stability and keep the car planted through the fast straights and heavy braking zones.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the front wing’s flap sections and the brake‑duct exits to give the car a more stable front end and better brake cooling, which should translate into smoother corner entry and fewer reliability worries. On the floor they’ve added a small edge trim and reshaped the forward floor pieces to boost down‑force without adding drag, while a new cooling‑exit panel on the engine cover helps keep the power unit running cooler. Together, these changes aim to improve grip and keep the car reliable for the upcoming weekend’s high‑speed laps.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has reshaped the front‑corner airflow by fitting a new, more aggressively‑shaped cooling scoop, which should keep the front tyres and brakes at optimal temperatures on this circuit. The front‑suspension bodywork has been tweaked to smooth the air over the wheels, giving the car a steadier front end and better grip out of the corners. Finally, the exhaust pipe has been moved slightly, helping to fine‑tune the rear‑end balance and give a little extra push on the straights.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has reshaped the car’s floor and tweaked a few aerodynamic bits – the main floor now has a fresh shape, the rear‑corner stall devices and the beam‑wing have been re‑profiled, and even the exhaust‑tailpipe bracket got a new contour. These changes tighten airflow and boost down‑force where it counts, giving the RB better grip and stability through the corners. In short, the car should feel more planted and responsive this weekend, especially on the high‑speed sections.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has reshaped the side‑pod inlet and its surrounding parts to smooth the air that rushes over the car, giving the engine cooler, more consistent airflow and a tighter rear‑end feel. The tweaks also help balance the car’s load around the floor and rear suspension, which should translate into a steadier grip through fast corners. In short, a cleaner‑flowing pod means a bit more power and better handling for this weekend’s race.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s new front‑ and rear‑brake duct shapes are tuned for this circuit, helping the car stay cooler under heavy braking and keep the tires in the optimal window. A reshaped diffuser winglet and fresh side‑pod louvers boost rear‑end grip, giving the car a steadier push through the high‑speed corners. Together, the changes should translate into more consistent lap times and a better fight for position over the weekend.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has reshaped the underside of the car and its rear wing, giving the floor a slightly different angle and the wing a tweaked profile. Those tweaks aim to improve how the car sticks to the track and manage airflow more efficiently, which should translate into better corner grip and a higher top‑speed straight. In short, the changes are designed to give Alpine a little extra downforce where it counts most for this weekend’s circuit.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has reshaped the front of the car – tweaking the very edge and the brake‑cooling passages – so the brakes stay cooler and the front end sticks to the track better. At the back they’ve refined the little winglet on the diffuser, tightening its shape to give a steadier push of downforce through the corners. Together, these tweaks should keep the car more stable and quicker over the whole lap this weekend.
